title: Evaluating the Impact of AI Tools on Language Proficiency and Intercultural Communication in Second Language Education
venue: International Journal of Second and Foreign Language Education
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether AI-driven language learning tools can improve second-language proficiency and intercultural communication, and what challenges arise when integrating them into education. The study is motivated by growing use of AI in language education and asks how effective tools such as Duolingo, Rosetta Stone, and ChatGPT are for language learning, whether they support intercultural competence, and what ethical or practical concerns accompany their use.

The author uses a mixed-methods design that combines structured online surveys with semi-structured interviews. The sample included 200 participants: 120 educators, 50 students, and 30 app developers. Quantitative survey data captured tool usage, perceived effectiveness, and satisfaction, while qualitative interviews explored participant experiences in more depth. The paper also includes a case example from a multicultural Canadian public school in which Duolingo was used over one semester to support English and French learning.

The study context is second-language education across varied educational settings, with participants selected purposively to represent different levels of proficiency and technological expertise. Students and educators both reported frequent use of AI tools, though students rated the tools as slightly more effective and satisfying than educators did. Teachers valued personalization and engagement but worried about over-reliance on AI and insufficient support for deeper cultural learning; students appreciated interactive dialogue practice and gamified learning; developers emphasized the need for more culturally immersive and interactive content.

Overall, the paper concludes that AI tools can effectively support language learning and intercultural communication when used as supplements to traditional instruction rather than replacements for human educators. The findings suggest benefits in personalization, flexibility, and conversational practice, but also highlight limitations related to self-reported outcomes, lack of long-term evidence, possible AI bias, privacy concerns, and unequal access. The paper recommends thoughtful curricular integration, ongoing teacher training, and future longitudinal research on sustained language and cultural outcomes.

identified_tools.name: Duolingo
identified_tools.description: A named AI-driven language learning app that provides gamified, personalized language practice.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as one of the AI-driven tools used in second language education; also featured in a semester-long case study in a multicultural Canadian public school to support English and French proficiency through personalized tasks.

findings.finding_summary: In a case study conducted over one semester in a multicultural Canadian public school, students used Duolingo for personalized English and French tasks and the paper reports significant improvements in language proficiency. No effect size, test name, or subgroup sample size for the Duolingo case study was reported.
findings.measure: Language proficiency in English and French after one semester of Duolingo use

findings.finding_summary: The Duolingo case study also reported significant improvements in student engagement levels over one semester. The paper does not provide a quantitative engagement measure, effect size, or sample size for this case study.

identified_tools.name: Rosetta Stone
identified_tools.description: A named AI-driven language learning platform using immersive language instruction approaches.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as one of the AI-driven tools in second language education; discussed particularly for its immersive approach supporting multiple dimensions of language proficiency.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: An OpenAI conversational AI system used for interactive dialogue and language practice.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as one of the AI-driven tools in second language education, especially for vocabulary building, grammar practice, and simulated culturally contextualized conversations.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an empirical mixed-methods study with surveys, interviews, and a case study, but the reported results are largely self-reported and descriptive, with limited tool-specific outcome reporting and no effect sizes for the named tools.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports positive impacts, including significant improvement in Duolingo-related language proficiency and engagement, but the magnitude of impact is unclear because effect sizes, confidence intervals, and case-study sample sizes are not reported.
